questionText:
Which of the following is/are the eigenvector(s) for the matrix given below?

$$\begin{pmatrix} -9 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ -8 & -6 & -3 & -1 \\ 20 & 15 & 8 & 5 \\ 32 & 21 & 7 & 12 \end{pmatrix}$$
explanation:
Definition: A non-zero vector $v$ is an eigenvector of a matrix $A$ if $Av = \lambda v$ for some scalar eigenvalue $\lambda$.

Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} -9 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ -8 & -6 & -3 & -1 \\ 20 & 15 & 8 & 5 \\ 32 & 21 & 7 & 12 \end{pmatrix}$.

Checking Option A:
$A \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (-9)(-1) + (-6)(1) + (-2)(0) + (-4)(1) \\ (-8)(-1) + (-6)(1) + (-3)(0) + (-1)(1) \\ (20)(-1) + (15)(1) + (8)(0) + (5)(1) \\ (32)(-1) + (21)(1) + (7)(0) + (12)(1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = 1 \cdot \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$
This satisfies $Av = 1 \cdot v$. Thus, Option A is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda = 1$.

Checking Option B:
$A \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (-9)(1) + (-2)(-1) \\ (-8)(1) + (-3)(-1) \\ (20)(1) + (8)(-1) \\ (32)(1) + (7)(-1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -7 \\ -5 \\ 12 \\ 25 \end{pmatrix} \neq \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$
Thus, Option B is NOT an eigenvector.

Checking Option C:
$A \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (-9)(-1) + (-2)(2) + (-4)(2) \\ (-8)(-1) + (-3)(2) + (-1)(2) \\ (20)(-1) + (8)(2) + (5)(2) \\ (32)(-1) + (7)(2) + (12)(2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} = 3 \cdot \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$
This satisfies $Av = 3 \cdot v$. Thus, Option C is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda = 3$.

Checking Option D:
$A \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (-6)(1) + (-2)(-3) \\ (-6)(1) + (-3)(-3) \\ (15)(1) + (8)(-3) \\ (21)(1) + (7)(-3) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ -9 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = 3 \cdot \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$
This satisfies $Av = 3 \cdot v$. Thus, Option D is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda = 3$.

Hence, options A, C, and D are correct.
